The ADHD assessment population (ADHD-udredningspopulation) in this dataset is analyzed across age groups, gender, and Danish regions based on a 2023 report [^src1]. Because the data consists of a single dated section, no longitudinal trends can be established.

In terms of age distribution, the 11–17 years cohort represents the largest share of assessments with 2,796 cases, while the 0–5 years cohort is the smallest with 405 cases [^src1]. The 6–10 years group falls in between with 2,014 assessments, bringing the total number of assessments to 5,215 [^src1]. 

Gender distribution reveals a notable outlier depending on the age group. While boys dominate the younger cohorts—accounting for 77% of assessments in the 0–5 years group and 73% in the 6–10 years group—the pattern reverses in the 11–17 years group, where girls make up 54% of the assessments compared to 46% for boys [^src1]. Overall, boys account for 59% of the total assessments and girls for 41% [^src1].

Geographically, [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] is the clear leader, accounting for 2,321 of the total assessments [^src1]. [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] follows with 1,171 assessments, and [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] records 701 [^src1]. The trailers in terms of assessment volume are [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] with 610 assessments and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] with the lowest total at 412 [^src1].

Summary: Tabellen præsenterer antal udredningsforløb fordelt på aldersgrupper, køn og regioner, og viser at Region Hovedstaden har flest udredningsforløb (2.321), mens flest forløb forekommer i aldersgruppen 11–17 år (2.796).
